dependencies.name: re

candidate.name: regex
candidate.coverage: 5/5 uses. PASCAL_RE (:9, :38) as-is with replace_all and a closure. re.sub(r"\s+") (:216) as [\s\x1C-\x1F]+. SPLIT_RE (:10, :252) through a find_iter helper that keeps the matches. ACRONYM_RE (:8, :240) and UNDERSCORE_RE (:11, :65, :93): lookarounds rewritten by hand around find_iter. No pattern needs fancy-regex.
candidate.evidence: cache/registry/crates/regex.json (lookup 2026-10-20). docs.rs regex 1.13.1: \d is \p{Nd}, \s is \p{White_Space}, no look-around, $ is end of haystack. Scout probe scratchpad/scout-re-probe: 45,559 inputs, 0 mismatches against CPython 3.14.6.

dependencies.notes: regex crate with lookarounds rewritten by hand; fancy-regex not used for any pattern. Cargo: regex = { version = "1.13", default-features = false, features = ["std", "unicode-perl"] }. Compile patterns once in std::sync::LazyLock (Rust 1.80+). Python \s is White_Space plus U+001C..U+001F; translate as [\s\x1C-\x1F]. Python \d and the crate's \d agree on Python 3.14 (Unicode 16); record fixtures with Python 3.14. Lookbehind in UNDERSCORE_RE must not be rewritten as a consuming group ("a_b_c" would give aB_c instead of aBC).

dependencies.name: collections.abc.Mapping

candidate.name: serde_json
candidate.coverage: Full for str-keyed dicts and lists: Value::Object = Mapping, Value::Array = list, Map iteration in insertion order with preserve_order, Map::insert = dict-comprehension assignment (later value wins, key keeps first position), Map PartialEq order-insensitive like dict ==. Not covered: non-str keys, tuple vs list, Mapping subclasses, unbounded ints, NaN/Infinity.
candidate.evidence: cache/registry/crates/serde_json.json and indexmap.json (lookup 2026-10-20). Scout probes: insertion order, collision position, equality.

dependencies.notes: Dict and list inputs map to serde_json::Value (user's package decision), so serde_json is a runtime dependency. Runtime features = ["preserve_order"] (without it Map is a BTreeMap and keys come out sorted). Dev/harness: features = ["preserve_order", "float_roundtrip"] (default float parsing misread about 10% of Python float reprs by 1 ULP in the scout probe). Never Map::remove in place (swap_remove reorders). Divergences to record in the contract: non-str keys unrepresentable; tuples not walked in Python but every JSON array is walked in Rust; top-level null/bool/number go through the Python string path; NaN/Infinity and ints beyond 64 bits not representable.
